name: Junk removal
summary: Start a junk removal business: your first 25 neighbors and partners, a price menu by truck load from real ranges, a load estimate from a list of items, and the dump rules to check where you live.
door_step3: I load it, haul it and sweep up
door_rule: Door hangers go on the door, never in or on a mailbox: putting unstamped flyers in a mailbox is a federal offense (18 U.S. Code 1725). Check your city rules on door to door flyers.

promises.first_25: 15 people you know and 10 local property managers, agents, estate sale shops, storage sites and contractors, each with a message, plus door hangers.
promises.offer: Your price menu by truck load, the first-clients ladder, add-ons for appliances and tires, and job math, on a one-page offer sheet.
promises.quote: How much of the truck, stairs, debris and appliances in; a quote, a text and an invoice out.
promises.keep: A thank-you, an honest review ask, a referral ask and a later check-in, each dated, plus review cards with your QR code.
promises.sample_one: A free demo for one street or one partner business: door hangers or a sample letter, a card to send and every message, saved to your Pipeline.
promises.reply: Paste what someone wrote back: what they meant, a short answer with one next step, and your Pipeline updated. A draft you send yourself.
promises.won: Log the yes, then everything for the job: the booking text, a prep text, a printable job sheet, the after-job text and the invoice.
promises.proof: One cleared garage turned into proof: a result card, a before-and-after collage, a caption, an honest review ask and a case study once they say yes.
promises.next_25: The next 25 property managers, agents, estate sale shops, storage sites and contractors near you, not yet in your Pipeline, with messages for Do my day.
promises.ready: Look ready before you reach out: a one-page website, a Google profile kit and a flyer, all from your real prices.
promises.same_street: One customer's street turned into a route: door hangers with a neighbor price, a sheet for the 20 nearest homes and an intro ask for your customer.
promises.load_estimate: A pasted list of items in; the share of the truck, the price, what needs special disposal where you live and the dump fee out, with a quote and invoice.

off_season.play: Work move-outs and estate cleanouts with property managers and estate sale shops, and presell spring garage cleanouts at this year's price.

crowd.note: Busiest March to October, peaking April to June (LawnStarter).
not_yet: Don't buy a dump truck or a big trailer before your tenth paid load.
Don't haul paint, chemicals, propane tanks or tires until you know your county's rules.
Don't take a fridge, freezer or AC unit until you know who recovers the refrigerant.
crowd.basis: Scores, first $1, buyer and not-yet lines: research/niches/junk.json crowd_scores (our judgment). Best months and slow season: LawnStarter says junk removal is busiest March through October, peaking April through June.

items.what_to_check: A truck, or a truck and trailer, rated 10,001 pounds or more used across state lines is a commercial motor vehicle under federal rules, and its carrier registers with FMCSA (USDOT number). Some states have similar rules for in-state work: check your state DOT.

sources.says: Commercial motor vehicle: a self-propelled or towed motor vehicle used on a highway in interstate commerce to transport passengers or property when it has a gross vehicle weight rating or gross combination weight rating, or gross vehicle weight or gross combination weight, of 10,001 pounds or more.
Each motor carrier (including a private motor carrier) subject to these requirements must file Form MCSA-1, the Unified Registration System application, with FMCSA (USDOT registration).

items.what_to_check: Washington requires a load to be secured so nothing drops or escapes (RCW 46.61.655), and Snohomish County charges an unsecured load fee at its stations. Check your state and county.

items.what_to_check: The final disposer recovers the refrigerant, or gets a signed statement saying who did and when (EPA Section 608). Ask your scrap yard or transfer station what they need.

sources.says: The final disposer of appliances is responsible for recovering any refrigerant contained in appliances. If someone other than the final disposer recovers the refrigerant, EPA requires a signed statement containing the name and address of the person who recovered the refrigerant and the date of recovery.

items.what_to_check: Many states ban whole tires from landfills (EPA). California requires a waste tire hauler registration to carry 10 or more used tires (CalRecycle). Check your state.

sources.publisher: U.S. EPA, Automobiles, Tires and Boats
sources.says: Many states ban all tires or whole tires from landfills. Check with your local and state waste officials about storage, handling or management requirements for scrap tires.

State law requires every person who transports 10 or more used or waste tires to hold a valid waste tire hauler registration, renewed each year, and to follow the used and waste tire manifest program.

items.what_to_check: Household hazardous waste goes to county collection, not the trash; paint goes to PaintCare sites in PaintCare states; propane rules differ by county. Check your county.

sources.says: Products such as paints, cleaners, oils, batteries and pesticides can contain hazardous ingredients. Many communities have collection programs for HHW; check with your local environmental, health or solid waste agency. Improper disposal includes, in some cases, putting them out with the regular trash.

Return lead-acid batteries to a battery retailer or local household hazardous waste collection program; do not put lead-acid batteries in the trash or municipal recycling bins. To prevent fires from lithium-ion batteries, tape battery terminals and never put these batteries in household garbage or recycling bins. Check with your local or state solid waste authority.

In states with paint stewardship laws, PaintCare operates paint recycling programs: California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Minnesota, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, Vermont and Washington. Find a drop-off site.
King County Solid Waste transfer stations do not accept propane tanks of any size; containers must be 8 gallons or less at its hazardous waste sites.

steps: Before the job: the price in writing from a photo or the Load estimate, what goes and what stays, where to park, and the paint, chemicals and propane that stay out.
On arrival: walk the pile with the owner, confirm the price before you load anything, and point out anything you cannot take.
Photograph the pile from two sides and anything already damaged nearby.
Set aside anything for donation or scrap metal, then load heavy and flat items first.
Pad door frames and corners, and use a dolly on stairs.
Cover or tie down the load before you drive.
Sweep the space, take the after photos from the same spots, and invoice the same day.

objections.objection: I could rent a truck and do it myself.
objections.answer: Fair, and some people do. Fixr says hauling it yourself can be difficult, time-consuming and expensive without a proper truck and a place to dump it. With you it is loaded, hauled and swept in one visit, at a price set before you load anything.

sources.says: Doing it yourself, hauling can be difficult, time-consuming, and expensive without a proper truck and disposal access; call your local landfill and find out how much it costs to drop off your junk.

objections.say: That's fair, and some people do. With me there's no truck to rent, nothing to lift and no dump run: I load it, haul it and sweep up in one visit, and you get the price before I load anything. Want me to price it from a photo so you can compare?

objections.objection: Will you take everything, even paint and chemicals?

keep.checkin: Hi {customer}, it's {first} from {business}. It's been a few months since your {job}. If the garage is filling up again, want me to save you a spot in the next couple of weeks?
keep.card_ask: How did it go? Scan to leave an honest review. Good or bad, it helps.
keep.rules: Ask every customer for a review, happy or not, and never offer a discount, gift or anything else for one; Google's rules forbid it. Only share photos the customer said yes to.

load.title: How much of the truck
load.description: Not sure? Run "Load estimate" on their list of items.

fridges.title: Fridges, freezers or AC units (optional)
fridges.description: How many. Each one adds the refrigerant fee.

advice.say: Heavy debris fills the truck by weight before it fills it by space: check your truck's payload, and ask your transfer station whether it charges more for construction debris.
Stairs or a long carry: bring a helper and a dolly, and walk the path before you price it.
Appliances with refrigerant: the refrigerant has to be recovered before disposal (EPA Section 608). Ask your scrap yard or transfer station what they charge and what they need.
Hot tub: ask the owner to have the power shut off and disconnected before you come, bring a helper and a saw, and price it after you see the path out (judgment call).
Piano: bring a helper, a piano dolly and straps, and check the stairs and doorways before you price it.

won.needs: the address, where the items are (curb, garage or upstairs), where I can park the truck, and a photo of the pile
prep_items: set aside anything you want to keep, and show me what goes
clear a path to the pile and a spot to park the truck close by
keep paint, chemicals, propane tanks and batteries out of the pile
empty and unplug any fridge or freezer the day before
bring: Truck or trailer, with a tarp and straps to cover the load
Dolly, hand truck and moving blankets
Work gloves, safety glasses and boots
Broom, shovel, contractor bags and a tape measure
Your price sheet and the estimate
photos: The pile before you touch it, from two sides
Walls, floors and door frames near the pile, before you start
The truck bed loaded, before you cover it
The swept space, from the same spots

proof.result: Garage cleared and swept, two chairs set aside for donation
proof.private: No faces, house numbers or license plates.

street.headline: One item hauled free on {street}
includes: One bulky item: a chair, a mattress or a grill
Loaded from the curb, driveway or garage
how: Text me your address and a photo of the item
I pick it up while I'm on {street}{day_part}
You see what it costs to clear the rest
street.line: I'm hauling a load on {street}{day_part}, so the first 3 neighbors who text me get one bulky item hauled away free, from the curb or garage: no cost and no catch. No paint, chemicals, tires or appliances with refrigerant.
street.post: Hi neighbors! I'm {first}, I run {business} here in {area}. I'm hauling on {street}{day_part}, so the first 3 neighbors who text me get one bulky item hauled away free from the curb or garage. No cost and no catch. {phone_line}
steps: Hang the door hangers on {street} the day before, on the door, never in or on a mailbox.
Pick up the first 3 items that are texted, and take a photo before and after.
Hand each neighbor your price sheet before you leave.
Text a thank-you the same day with the photo, then one follow-up in 3 days.

property_managers.demo: one small load, up to 1/8 of my truck, hauled from a unit you manage
property_managers.headline: Move-out leftovers hauled away and swept up
property_managers.card_line: For units {biz} manages: book through your property manager.
steps: Send the message and the card today.
Ask which unit turns over next and the day it must be empty.
Haul only what the manager confirms in writing can go, then photograph the swept room from the doorway.
Send the photos the same day for their file.

realtors.demo: one small load, up to 1/8 of my truck, hauled from a listing you're getting ready
realtors.headline: Garage cleared before the listing photos
steps: Send the message and the card today.
Ask which listing has a garage, basement or shed to clear, and the photo day.
Haul only what the seller marked to go, and photograph before and after from the same spot.
Send the agent the photos the same day.

estate_sales.demo: one small load, up to 1/8 of my truck, of what's left after one of your sales
estate_sales.headline: What didn't sell, hauled away
steps: Send the message and the card today.
Ask for the address, the day after the sale, and what stays.
Set aside anything they can still sell, haul the rest and sweep up.
Send the before and after photos the same day.

self_storage.demo: one small load, up to 1/8 of my truck, hauled from a unit you need emptied
self_storage.headline: Moving out? Leave the junk to me
steps: Send the message and the card today.
Ask the manager for one unit they need emptied and the gate hours.
Haul only what the manager confirms in writing can go, and photograph the swept unit.
Leave a few cards at the front desk if they said yes.

contractors.demo: one small load of debris, up to 1/8 of my truck, hauled from one of your job sites
contractors.headline: Remodel debris hauled away, no dumpster in the driveway
steps: Send the message and the card today.
Check your transfer station's price for construction debris first: some charge extra for it.
Haul one small pile, sweep the site and photograph before and after.
Send the photos the same day.

same_street.neighbor_note: judgment call, not a sourced fact
same_street.headline: Your neighbor price on {street}
includes: Loaded from the curb, driveway or garage
how: Text me your address and a photo of the pile
You get the price before I load anything
same_street.customer_ask: Hi {customer}, thanks again! I'm hauling on {street}{day_part} and have room for a couple more loads. If a neighbor ever asks who cleared your garage, would you pass on my number{phone_part}? It means a lot to a new business.
steps: Hang a door hanger on every home on this sheet the day before you haul there. On the door, never in or on a mailbox.
While you load, say hi to anyone outside. Keep it short, and never say which neighbor: "I'm hauling a load for a home on your street."
Text your customer the intro ask after the job, never before.
Mark each home on the sheet. A neighbor who books goes on the same day as your customer, while the truck has room.
same_street.why: When the truck is already on the street with room to spare, a neighbor's load adds little driving, so you can give neighbors a better price on the same day.
